QuestionStmt.S: The distance of the point $(2, 4, 0)$ from the point of intersection of the lines $$\frac{x+6}{3} = \frac{y}{2} = \frac{z+1}{1}$$ and $$\frac{x-7}{4} = \frac{y-9}{3} = \frac{z-4}{2}$$ is

Solution.S:
Let $\frac{x+6}{3} = \frac{y}{2} = \frac{z+1}{1} = t$ and $\frac{x-7}{4} = \frac{y-9}{3} = \frac{z-4}{2} = s$.

$$\Rightarrow x = 3t - 6, y = 2t, z = t - 1 \quad \dots (i)$$

and $x = 4s + 7, y = 3s + 9, z = 2s + 4$.

Since the given lines intersect each other,

$$3t - 6 = 4s + 7 \Rightarrow 3t - 4s = 13 \quad \dots (ii)$$

$$2t = 3s + 9 \Rightarrow 2t - 3s = 9 \quad \dots (iii)$$

$$t - 1 = 2s + 4 \Rightarrow t - 2s = 5 \quad \dots (iv)$$

From (ii) and (iv), we get $t = 3, s = -1$.

Substituting the value of $t$ in (i), we get $x = 3, y = 6, z = 2$.

$$\therefore \text{ The point of intersection of the given lines is } (3, 6, 2).$$

$$\therefore \text{ Required distance } = \sqrt{(3 - 2)^2 + (6 - 4)^2 + (2 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3 \text{ units}$$
